meaning: A rare bloom of good fortune
title: Chrysanthemum also known as Fossil Coral is a natural type of gemstone formed by ancient corals.
sub: The proper name for fossil coral is ‘agatized coral’ or ‘agatized fossil coral’, because during formation, the coral remains are gradually replaced with agate, a variety of naturally occurring chalcedony, or microcrystalline quartz.

intro.text: When prehistoric corals are fossilized through replacement with agate, the fossil coral forms through hardened deposits left by silica-rich waters. The entire process can take over 20 million years and occurs only under very unique geological conditions.
Corals are marine animals and it is their skeletons that are fossilized and preserved, often leaving flower-like patterns in the stone.

The oldest coral fossils are over 500 million years old. The earliest forms were different from those we see today and they died out 225 million years ago. Modern corals are still common in tropical oceans. These are solitary corals from the Jurassic and Cretaceous periods. Chrysanthemum can be color enhanced.

name: Picture Jasper
title: Picture jasper is like looking into the Earth.
sub: Picture Jasper is a brown colored jasper with a mixture of tans, browns, cream, and grey.

intro.text: It empowers your inner Earth energy, to go to places or times in the past. Connect yourself to sacred places. It is a very good stone to use when you are working with dreams or visioning.

name: Red Carnelian
title: Red Carnelian
sub: Heat with discipline. Red Carnelian is not subtle, and it’s not trying to be.

intro.text: Its color comes from iron-rich silica, formed slowly, then intensified by natural heat in the earth.

intro.label: Provenance
intro.text: Indonesia, Brazil, India, Russia (Siberia), and Germany.

intro.label: Why wear Red Carnelian?
intro.text: Because energy doesn’t need noise. Because warmth can be controlled. Because strength doesn’t have to be dark.

name: Red Garnet
title: Red Garnet
sub: Density over display. Red Garnet doesn’t glow. It holds weight.

intro.text: This is a mineral formed under intense pressure. Garnet crystals grow dense, not flashy. That density is exactly why good Garnet feels serious.

intro.label: Provenance
intro.text: Brazil, India, Madagascar, Sri Lanka and the USA. Smaller deposits exist in Austria and the Czech Republic.

intro.label: Why wear Red Garnet?
intro.text: Because depth beats shine. Because intensity doesn’t need brightness. Because authority is quiet.

name: Rhyolite
title: Rhyolite
sub: Volcanic complexity, controlled. Rhyolite is volcanic rock that refuses simplicity.

intro.text: Formed from silica-rich lava, it cools slower than basalt, allowing minerals to separate, flow, and reorganize. The result is layered color, mottled texture, and complex patterning that looks almost engineered — but isn’t.

intro.label: Provenance
intro.text: France, Germany, Andes, Yellowstone, New Zealand, India.

intro.label: Why wear Rhyolite?
intro.text: Because complexity can be calm. Because structure doesn’t have to be minimal. Because natural systems outperform forced design.

name: Rose Quartz
title: Rose Quartz
sub: Strength without noise. Rose Quartz is carrying color through iron and titanium traces locked into the crystal.

intro.text: Good Rose Quartz has a milky depth, not transparency. Light enters and diffuses slowly, giving the stone a calm, solid presence.

intro.label: Provenance
intro.text: Madagascar, India, Germany, South Dakota USA, Brazil.

intro.label: Why wear Rose Quartz?
intro.text: Because confidence doesn’t need darkness. Because calm is not weakness. Because presence can be quiet.

name: Rutilated Quartz
title: Rutilated Quartz
sub: Order pierced by light. Rutilated Quartz is quartz interrupted — deliberately.

intro.text: Inside the crystal, fine needles of rutile grow in straight, angular lines, cutting through the clear body like metal under glass. These inclusions are not defects. They are the entire point.

intro.label: Provenance
intro.text: Australia, Brazil, Kazakhstan, Madagascar, Norway, Pakistan and the United States.

intro.label: Why wear Rutilated Quartz?
intro.text: Because clarity doesn’t mean emptiness. Because strength shows through contrast. Because complexity can be disciplined.

name: Sea Sediment Jasper
title: Sea Sediment Jasper
sub: Controlled color. Honest craftsmanship. Stabilized sea sediment jasper, a material created by compressing natural sedimentary stone and reinforcing it for long-term stability

intro.text: Sea Sediment Jasper: The blue and red tones are intentionally enhanced. They are not the result of geological coincidence, but of controlled treatment to achieve balance, contrast, and repeatable quality.

intro.label: Why choose this bracelet?
intro.text: Because transparency matters. Because design doesn’t need myths to be valuable. Because craftsmanship and honesty age better than exaggeration.

name: Sodalite
title: Sodalite
sub: Blue, stripped of excess. Deep navy tones cut by sharp white calcite veins. No sparkle. No surface tricks. Just contrast, structure, and restraint.

intro.text: This is a stone chosen by people who prefer clarity over gloss. The blue is dense and matte, closer to ink or midnight stone than anything polished or flashy.

intro.label: Provenance
intro.text: USA, Namibia, Canada, Russia, Greenland.

intro.label: Why wear Sodalite?
intro.text: Because discipline outlasts noise. Because contrast creates order. Because depth doesn’t need gloss.

name: Strawberry Quartz
title: Strawberry Quartz
sub: Color held in clarity. The color lives inside the crystal, not on the surface.

intro.text: Good Strawberry Quartz shows depth and distribution. The inclusions are visible but controlled, floating rather than clumping.

intro.label: Provenance
intro.text: Mexico, Africa, Russia.

intro.label: Why wear Strawberry Quartz?
intro.text: Because warmth doesn’t need gloss. Because clarity makes color credible. Because subtle complexity lasts longer than bold effects.

name: Sunstone
title: Sunstone
sub: Light, disciplined. Sunstone doesn’t glitter. It radiates from within.

intro.text: Tiny mineral platelets, usually copper or hematite, are locked inside the feldspar crystal. When light moves, those inclusions ignite a soft internal flash called aventurescence. Not surface sparkle. Structural glow.

intro.label: Provenance
intro.text: United States (Oregon), India, Tanzania, Norway.

intro.label: Why wear Sunstone?
intro.text: Because warmth doesn’t need excess. Because light is strongest when it’s controlled. Because presence can be subtle and still powerful.

name: Swarovski
title: Swarovski
sub: Precision, engineered. Swarovski is not a gemstone. It’s engineered crystal, perfected through precision, chemistry, and control.

intro.text: Founded in Austria in 1895, Swarovski developed a proprietary method for cutting lead crystal with extreme accuracy. The result is a material that behaves differently from natural stone: sharper facets, higher brilliance, and absolute consistency.

intro.label: Provenance
intro.text: Austria.

intro.label: Why choose Swarovski?
intro.text: Because precision is a form of luxury. Because modern design doesn’t need myths. Because brilliance can be engineered honestly.

name: Tiger's Eye
title: Tiger’s Eye
sub: Movement with authority. Tiger’s Eye is defined by motion. Not shine. Not sparkle. Movement.

intro.text: When light hits the stone, a sharp band slides across the surface. That optical effect—chatoyancy—comes from fibrous structures locked inside the quartz. It’s structural, not decorative.

intro.label: Provenance
intro.text: South Africa and Western Australia.

intro.label: Why wear Tiger’s Eye?
intro.text: Because confidence is dynamic. Because control beats aggression. Because presence should respond, not shout.

name: Tridacna
title: Tridacna
sub: Marine origin. Minimal presence.

intro.text: Tridacna is not a gemstone. It’s shell, cut from the inner layer of the giant clam (Tridacna species). Dense, matte, and naturally white, with a soft grain that feels organic rather than polished.

intro.label: Provenance
intro.text: Mediterranean Sea and Indo-Pacific Ocean.

intro.label: Why wear Tridacna?
intro.text: Because restraint is powerful. Because not everything needs to sparkle. Because calm materials elevate strong design.

name: Turquoise
title: Turquoise
sub: Color with lineage Turquoise is one of the few stones where color is identity.

intro.text: Not surface color. Not treatment shine. Real turquoise carries its blue-green tone through the entire stone, shaped by copper-rich fluids binding mineral fragments over time.

intro.label: Provenance
intro.text: Iran (Nishapur), United States (Arizona, Nevada), Mexico, China / Tibet.

intro.label: Why wear Turquoise?
intro.text: Because real color doesn’t fade quietly. Because heritage matters when the material carries it. Because authenticity beats intensity.

name: Turquoise Calsilica
title: Turquoise Calsilica
sub: Color, stabilized by design. Turquoise Calsilica is not traditional turquoise.

intro.text: It’s a stabilized composite material, created by combining natural turquoise fragments with calcium-based minerals and silica, then compressing the mix into a dense, workable stone.

intro.label: Why choose Turquoise Calsilica?
intro.text: Because durability matters. Because consistency can be intentional. Because transparency builds trust.
